name: F&G ANNUITIES AND LIFE INC

priced.reason: book method needs rotce_override or final_growth

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The strongest counter is that the refusal is now costing real money: the stock is 33% lower over twelve months and 26% lower than when this engine last refused it, and on EVERY defensible denominator it looks cheap. Price to ex-AOCI book is 0.43x; price to GAAP book 0.59x; price to LTM adjusted earnings roughly 5.3x on an 8.0% rolling-four-quarter adjusted ROE applied to approximately $6.0 billion of ex-AOCI common equity. A justified price-to-book of (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) gives 0.77x on 8% ROE against a 9.75% cost of equity and 2% growth, which is +82% against the actual 0.43x; on GAAP book, where the same adjusted earnings imply an 11.1% return, it gives 1.17x against 0.59x, or +100%. Three independent framings all say cheap. Refusing a name where every framing agrees on the sign looks like the engine protecting itself rather than answering.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: A sustainable adjusted ROE. Specifically, whether the alternative-investment portfolio of roughly $4.4 billion (implied by $55 million a quarter at a 5% annualised return) earns 5% or 12% through a cycle, because that single input is worth approximately $1.86 per share of annual adjusted earnings against roughly $3.70 of LTM adjusted earnings per share.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The settling evidence is visible and it BREAKS the counter, which is why the verdict does not move. The counter's three framings all assume an 8% or better ROE. Run the same justified-price-to-book formula at the ROE the current quarter implies — 5% — and it gives (5-2)/(9.75-2) = 0.39x against an actual 0.43x, i.e. the stock is RICH. So the sign does flip, on exactly the input the company told the market on 2026-10-05 is running at 42% of plan for the third quarter in a row. A defensible sustainable ROE between 5% and 11% spans a verdict from -10% to +100%. That is the JXN condition in research/LESSONS.md in its own words: when one defensible input choice moves the answer that far, the output is not a valuation. The devil's advocate here is the bear, and it is what keeps this off `cheap`.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I still cannot determine F&G's through-cycle alternative-investment return, which requires a view on the underlying limited-partnership and COLI portfolio that I have not built and cannot build from free sources. I also did not test whether ex-AOCI book is recoverable under surrender stress — the ex-AOCI measure assumes the bond portfolio is held to maturity, and a $1.66 billion negative AOCI is what the market would realise if it were not.

what_changed: The observable the last devil's-advocate pass on this name nominated has arrived, and it went AGAINST the bull case. On 2026-10-05 F&G furnished an 8-K (items 2.02 and 7.01) disclosing preliminary Q3 2026 investment income from alternative investments of approximately $47-57 million pre-tax. The midpoint represents AN ANNUALISED RETURN OF APPROXIMATELY 5% against management's stated long-term expected return of approximately 12%, leaving the quarter $70 million pre-tax and $55 million post-tax BELOW plan — roughly $0.42 per share in one quarter on 131 million shares. The 2026-09-04 verdict on this name said the bull case needed 'four to six quarters of adjusted ROE ex-AOCI printing 11%+ with alternative-investment returns at or above their long-run assumption'; this is the third consecutive quarter below it, the Q2 miss having been attributed to the same cause. Q3 results are scheduled for 2026-11-05. Barclays cut its target to $24 from $27.
consensus_case: F&G is a $75 billion-AUM fixed-indexed-annuity and pension-risk-transfer platform, 85% owned by FNF, and at $19.53 it trades at 0.43x its own reported ex-AOCI book value of $45.93 per share and 0.59x GAAP book of $33.27. The market pays that because spread-based annuity earnings are levered to credit and to alternative-investment returns that are currently running at a third of plan, because the float is small and the FNF overhang permanent, and because the most recent disclosed adjusted ROE excluding AOCI is 8.0% against a cost of equity near 9.8%. A company earning below its cost of capital is arithmetically worth less than book, and the market is applying that arithmetic. The 11.1% drop in five days and 17.4% in 21 days has a dated cause, disclosed by the company on 2026-10-05.
base_case_rationale: No base case and no sustainable ROTCE supplied, for the same reason as the 2026-09-04 pass and with better arithmetic behind it. The engine's model prices a sustainable ROTCE against tangible common equity; on a life and annuity writer both terms are artifacts, and the engine's inputs are unchanged from five weeks ago — still 31.7% ROTCE against $15.83 of tangible book per share. The company's own 2026-06-30 numbers are: total shareholders' equity $4,609M, less $250M preferred, giving common equity of $4,359M, of which AOCI is NEGATIVE $1,658M, so common equity excluding AOCI is $6,017M on 131 million shares. Supplying a `rotce_override` would price my number against the wrong denominator, which is worse than supplying none.
key_risks: Alternative-investment returns at 5% against a 12% long-term assumption, now for a third consecutive quarter
FIA spread compression if rates fall faster than crediting rates reset
$1.66 billion of negative AOCI — ex-AOCI book is only recoverable absent forced sales
FNF's ~85% ownership: minority holders control neither capital allocation nor a sale
Series A mandatory convertible preferred dilution
watch_for: Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-05 and the call on 11-06: whether management lowers the 12% long-term alternative-return assumption, which is the single input that decides this name
Adjusted ROE excluding AOCI sustaining above 11% for four consecutive quarters
Ex-AOCI book value per share stalling — it was $45.93 at 2026-06-30 against $46.51 at Q1 and $44.43 at year-end 2025, so it has already stopped compounding
Any FNF action on the stake (spin, buy-in, secondary)
